name: Today's districts (2025–26)
desc: The 32 community school districts as they exist today. They are very unequal in size: the largest has several times the enrollment of the smallest. Schools located outside their own district (like Beacon High School, District 3, located in District 2) are counted in the district they report to.

name: Equal size, compact
desc: A computer-generated example, redrawn from scratch with shapes as compact as possible and seats re-apportioned to boroughs by enrollment. Each district aims to be within 5% of its borough's average size; larger building blocks may not get there, so check the scorecard.

name: Economic balance
desc: A computer-generated example that brings each district's share of students in poverty as close to the citywide rate as geography allows. Each district aims to be within 5% of its borough's average size; larger building blocks may not get there, so check the scorecard.

name: Racial/ethnic integration
desc: A computer-generated example that brings each district's racial/ethnic mix as close to the city's as geography allows (minimizes Theil's H). Each district aims to be within 5% of its borough's average size; larger building blocks may not get there, so check the scorecard.

name: Balanced blend
desc: A computer-generated middle path: reasonably compact, with moderate weight on both economic and racial/ethnic balance. Each district aims to be within 5% of its borough's average size; larger building blocks may not get there, so check the scorecard.

name: Fix sizes, minimal change
desc: A computer-generated example that starts from today's map, keeps each borough's current number of districts, and moves as few students as possible toward equal size. Each district aims to be within 5% of its borough's average size; larger building blocks may not get there, so check the scorecard.
